name: Door Installation
description: Interior and exterior doors replaced in the existing opening, sticking doors adjusted, and hardware upgraded.
features: Entry and storm door replacement, same opening
Interior slab and prehung doors hung and cased
Deadbolts, keypad locks, and knob sets
Closet, bifold, and sliding doors re-tracked
Window sill and casing repair at the door

faqs.question: How long does it take to replace a door?
faqs.answer: A slab on an existing frame is an hour or two. A prehung interior door with new casing is closer to a half day, and an entry door with a threshold, weatherstripping, and lockset fills most of a half day. Two or three interior doors in one trip is normal, which is why it pays to batch them.

faqs.question: Is a permit needed to replace a door in Mercer County?
faqs.answer: Not when the new door goes into the same opening. New Jersey's construction code lists that as ordinary maintenance. Widening a doorway, cutting a new one, or changing the header is structural and would need a permit, and that is work we would refer out.

faqs.question: Why does my door stick or refuse to latch?
faqs.answer: Summer humidity swells wood, houses settle, hinge screws pull out of soft jambs, and strike plates drift. We find the cause before reaching for a new door. Nine times out of ten it is a longer hinge screw, a moved strike, or a pass with the plane, all of which fit in a Visit.

faqs.question: What exterior door holds up best in New Jersey weather?
faqs.answer: Fiberglass or steel over wood for most houses. Fiberglass will not warp or rot and the better ones look like real wood from the sidewalk. Steel is strong and insulates well. If you want wood for a historic front, we will tell you what maintenance it needs so you go in with open eyes.

name: Drywall Repair
description: Holes, cracks, water damage, and ceilings patched, taped, and blended so the repair disappears under paint.
features: Water-damaged board cut out and replaced
Texture matched, including popcorn and knockdown
Ceiling repairs and full sheet replacement
Plaster patched as plaster in older homes

faqs.question: How long does a drywall repair take?
faqs.answer: A patch under six inches is one visit for compound and a sand, then a day of drying before paint. Bigger holes and water damage need two or three coats with drying time between, so they run two to three days of short stops. Everything leaves primed and ready to paint, or painted if you have the color.

faqs.question: Can you match a textured or popcorn ceiling?
faqs.answer: Yes. Popcorn, orange peel, knockdown, and smooth are all doable, and a texture mismatch is the thing people notice from across the room, so we take the time to get it right before primer goes on.

faqs.question: Is my crack cosmetic or something worse?
faqs.answer: Nail pops, hairline cracks, small holes, and dings are cosmetic. Long diagonal cracks off the corners of doors and windows, cracks that come back after a repair, or a ceiling that sags are worth a closer look. We tell you which you have and repair it so it stays repaired, with mesh and setting compound where it counts.

faqs.question: The drywall got wet. Can it just be patched?
faqs.answer: Only if the source is fixed and the board is still firm. Soft, crumbling, or moldy drywall comes out and gets replaced; patching over it hides the problem for a season and then you pay twice. We check moisture before recommending anything.

name: Deck Staining
description: Wood decks washed, repaired, and stained or sealed so they hold up through Jersey winters.
features: Wash and prep before any stain
Soft and split boards replaced first
Scheduled around a dry weather window

faqs.question: How often should a deck be restained in this part of New Jersey?
faqs.answer: Every two to three years for most decks, sooner on a south- or west-facing deck that takes full sun. Pour a cup of water on a board: if it soaks in instead of beading, the sealer is gone and it is time.

faqs.question: What prep do you do before staining?
faqs.answer: Prep is most of the job. We wash off dirt, mildew, and failing stain, sand the rough boards, replace anything soft, and then let the wood dry for a day or two. Stain over a damp or dirty deck peels within a year, which is why we watch the forecast instead of the calendar.

faqs.question: Stain or paint?
faqs.answer: Stain, almost always. It soaks into the grain and breathes, so it wears instead of peeling in our humid summers. Paint sits on top, hides more, and eventually lifts, and then it has to be stripped before anything else goes on. Solid-color stain gets you most of paint's look without that problem.

faqs.question: Can you replace a few boards before staining?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we always do. Rotten or cracked boards come out, sound ones stay, and the whole surface gets stained together so the new wood does not stand out. A few boards and a stain is a fraction of what a new deck costs.

name: Fence Repair
description: Leaning posts reset, broken panels and pickets replaced, and gates rehung so they swing and latch.
features: Leaning posts dug out and reset in concrete

faqs.question: What fence problems do you see most around Princeton?
faqs.answer: Posts that heave and lean after a freeze-thaw winter, pickets and panels that let go at the fasteners, gates that sag until they drag, and hardware that rusts through. The clay soil in much of Mercer County moves a lot between seasons, and fence posts feel it first.

faqs.question: Does a leaning post need replacing?
faqs.answer: Not if it is still solid at the ground line. A post that leans but is not rotted gets dug out, plumbed, and set in fresh concrete. One that has broken at grade or crumbles when you push a screwdriver into it gets replaced, and we reuse the panels on either side when they are sound.

faqs.question: Can a gate that will not close be fixed?
faqs.answer: Almost always. Gates sag when hinges wear, the hinge post leans, or the frame racks out of square. We find which one it is, then rehang on new hinges, add a diagonal brace, or reset the post, and put on a latch that actually catches.

faqs.question: Do fence repairs need a permit?
faqs.answer: Repairs to an existing fence do not: replacing boards, resetting posts, fixing a gate. New fencing, or changing a fence's height or location, is regulated by each township's zoning rules. We do repairs, not new fence runs, so the permit question rarely comes up.
